plan.summary: Add an empty-audience guard in the greeting function so that an empty or whitespace-only audience is rejected before the greeting string is constructed, while preserving the existing happy path with a non-empty configured audience.
steps: Inspect src/greeting.py to identify where the greeting string is constructed.
Add an early guard that raises ValueError if audience is empty or whitespace-only.
Verify that the configured happy path (audience='traveler') still returns 'Welcome, traveler.'.
risks: Raising ValueError changes the error contract from always returning a string; callers that do not catch it will see an exception instead of a malformed greeting.

answer.summary: Added an empty/whitespace-only audience guard in greeting() that raises ValueError before constructing the greeting string, preserving the existing happy path for non-empty configured audiences.

argv: import subprocess,sys; happy=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-c","from src.greeting import greeting; assert greeting(\"traveler\") == \"Welcome, traveler.\""],capture_output=True,text=True); empty=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-c","from src.greeting import greeting; greeting(\"\")"],capture_output=True,text=True); assert happy.returncode == 0 and happy.stdout == "" and happy.stderr == ""; assert empty.returncode == 1 and empty.stdout == "" and "audience must not be empty" in empty.stderr
